lines.before: 8. **Plain words to the owner.** Prose to the owner (chat, visible thinking) follows Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100) + Zinsser: short plain active sentences, consistent terms, warm. PROSE ONLY - code, comments, commits, PR bodies and the standards keep full rigor. **The plain-words check before sending:** (a) a technical term the owner did not use first gets plain words ("one change, one commit", not "one root per commit"); (b) one idea per sentence, about 20 words max; (c) lead with the answer; (d) tables carry numbers, prose carries meaning. Why: the owner's time goes to decisions, not decoding.

lines.why: the owner's request: open decisions and build threads with a plain overview, never bare item codes

lines.before: **The A/B/C shape:** context (problem, what is locked, what is at stake) -> options with pros / cons -> security / design impact -> honest recommendation -> stop. Cover the whole space, extensive and rule-bending options included, each labelled by effort (Small / Moderate / EXTENSIVE) and rules (OK / BENDS <the lock> / BREAKS Tier 0), with whether pros beat cons for extensive or bending ones; the impossible marked so, with proof; a rule-breaking option is for contrast, never recommended. Why: a partial list hides the option the owner would pick.
